incident-bot: [ALERT] Incident INC-2026-043 created — elevated GPU memory pressure + model init failures in us-west-2. Affected pool: r5-gpu-prod-07. Severity: P1. Pager: @sre-oncall-alex

sre-oncall-alex: seeing a spike in OOMs during model load on several replicas. Root logs: `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (10.5GB requested)`, containers restarting repeatedly.

eng-runtime-emily: digging in — sequence is: artifact download -> decompress -> nvrtc kernel compile -> model init. We're seeing `zstd: decompression failed: checksum mismatch` immediately before compile attempts, then `nvrtc: timeout after 60s`. Sounds like corrupted artifact causes bad kernels and compile stalls.

infra-raj: node metrics show heavy host paging (swap usage ~22GB) coincident with the spike; disk io and CPU also climb. Containers are restarting (RestartCount++ ~3-5). Not seeing kernel OOM killer, just allocation failures in CUDA.

support-liz: customer impact check: two high-volume customers experienced 503s in the US region for ~4-7 minutes during peak. Support cases opened and triaged.

eng-runtime-emily: immediate mitigation plan: mark affected pool unhealthy so load balancer reroutes, scale up warm cache nodes to reduce concurrent inits, and enable artifact checksum retry/fallback.

sre-oncall-alex: applying mitigation now — cordoning problematic node and draining: `kubectl cordon gpu-07-12 && kubectl drain gpu-07-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Also updating routing rules to prefer canary/dedicated warm pool.

infra-raj: spun up 2 extra warm nodes in us-west-2 to take load. One node failed pulling the artifact due to checksum mismatch from the regional replica — initiating re-replication from primary.

eng-runtime-emily: deployed a temporary change to verify artifact checksum before decompress. If checksum fails, try alternate region pull and fallback to previous stable model version. Rolling out as canary to 10% traffic.

sre-oncall-alex: handoff: infra-raj owns storage replication investigation; eng-runtime-emily owns hotfix rollout and monitoring; support-liz to communicate customer updates.

support-liz: customer message sent: "We're investigating intermittent 503s caused by model initialization errors in us-west-2; traffic has been rerouted and mitigations are in place. We'll update once fully resolved."

infra-raj: found one bad S3 object replica in us-west-2 (single-part corruption). Re-replicated from primary replica and invalidated CDN edge cache for affected key. Increased S3 GET retries for artifact fetches temporally.

eng-runtime-emily: hotfix metrics: model init failure rate dropped from 12% to 0.8% over last 10m after checksum verification + fallback. Kernel compile timeouts have stopped on canary nodes.

sre-oncall-alex: monitoring window started for 30m. Next steps for RCA: why a corrupted S3 replica existed (storage pipeline/race), and why nvrtc compile didn't fail faster (improve timeout and fallback behavior).

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-043 status updated -> mitigated. Duration: 00:18:35. Runbook steps executed: reroute traffic, cordon/drain node, re-replicate artifact, deploy checksum fallback. Severity downgraded to P3.

eng-runtime-emily: created RCA ticket TKT-4321 (assigned to eng-runtime-emily and infra-raj). Items: artifact validation on publish, stronger pull-time fallback, reduce kernel compile timeout to fail-fast, add pre-download checks on warm nodes.

sre-oncall-alex: leaving on-call note: no further customer-impact observed after mitigations. Closing active handoff. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

support-liz: updating ticket with customer follow-ups and post-incident note.

eng-runtime-emily: post-mortem will include logs/snippets and a reproducible test for corrupted artifact -> compile timeout flow. Scheduling a short retro with infra next week.

sre-oncall-alex: closing thread. If anything recurs, reopen INC-2026-043 and ping channel. :heart:
